correctness.rationale: Exact Fourier aliasing of the Poisson kernel on an \(N\)-node grid gives a shifted \(P_{r^N}\) sample; Fourier orthogonality gives mean one and variance \(2q^2/[m(1-q^2)]\). Subcritical proof conditions on rare hits to an O(epsilon) arc and controls the tail expectation. At critical m epsilon -> lambda, a scaled Laplace integral converges by an integrable C/(1+x^2) bound to the homogeneous Poisson shot-noise functional, with Campbell moments 1 and 1/lambda. Above threshold, exact variance and bounded triangular-array summands give L2 convergence and a standard normal CLT. A bounded-subsequence argument proves necessity. The standalone VERIFIER.py was executed from its real package source path and passed 475 deterministic assertions; numerical tests are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact moving-boundary Poisson kernel is an analytically motivated stress model for periodic near-singular quadrature. With independent random origin shifts, it gives a sharp necessary-and-sufficient total grid-evaluation budget \(mN(1-r)\to\infty\), and distinguishes unbiasedness from concentration by proving typical collapse below threshold. The critical parameter produces a non-Gaussian Poisson shot-noise law with explicit Laplace transform and variance, and the strong-budget regime has a verified CLT; these give actionable accuracy-planning and implementation benchmarks. This is not merely a textbook aliasing formula because the probability limit and iff cross-regime necessity require additional arguments.
